prohibitions_observed: No source or historical evidence edits

claims.claim: Byte custody, numerical consistency, schema acceptance and mathematical validity are separate obligations.
limitations: Automated results never mark a data file as a full source review.
Hashes establish byte correspondence under their declared input convention, not a source event, theorem or model capability.

claims.claim: All 95 retained score records satisfy their strict model and weakest-gate/token/floor/mutation-ratio arithmetic, while custody checks can still fail.
dependencies: Mutation denominator killed+survived+inconclusive+unrun, excluding demonstrably equivalent and invalid mutants
limitations: The arithmetically weakest declared gate may itself be unjustified.
Historical scores and exemptions were not promoted into fresh source evidence.

claims.claim: The 25 retained v1 derivation/experiment runs and their 80 provider receipts pass the audited JSON arithmetic and internal binding checks.
dependencies: Per-stage output cap and recorded price ceiling
limitations: No database/private storage access, provider call or independent billing confirmation.
No prompt-lineage regeneration or observer/proposal mathematical check.
All terminal analytical_status values remain UNVERIFIED.

claims.claim: Tower loss histograms, producer commitments, declared census summaries and embedded fixture hashes can be checked without granting target authority.
dependencies: The producer classifies each loss field and each clause
limitations: A histogram does not validate the correctness of its semantic classifications.
Target injectivity, compatibility, goal/move correspondence and native proof claims were not established.
Broken envelope/content-address links are separately reported in ASE-F01.

claims.claim: All 17,503 original JSON/JSONL/YAML files were structurally parsed, but only 1,527 structured files received the selected schema-specific checks.
limitations: The 15,976 remaining structured files still require schema/semantic review.
Many additionally hashed sources have only referenced-byte evidence.
This supplement does not complete the every-file substantive audit.

findings.finding: Historical v2 tower content addresses and transport envelopes do not bind the retained bytes.

evidence.line_ending_diagnostic: All 108 filename mismatches persist against LF-normalized bytes and the pinned Git blobs; payload/record computations already use producer canonical serialization.

findings.impact: The digest-named v2 witness bundle and certificate custody chain cannot be used as intact byte evidence at this snapshot.
limitations: No cause or author is inferred. This is a retained-byte mismatch at the pinned inventory, not a claim that the historical run never occurred.
Loss-ledger commitments and all canonical serialization checks pass; no blanket claim that all tower evidence is corrupted.
findings.recommendation: Preserve the historical files; recover and identify the actual original bytes or issue a separately versioned reconstruction receipt before relying on these links.

findings.finding: All 216 generated transport certificates fail the current receiving transport schema despite sharing its schema identifier.
findings.impact: They remain drafts awaiting an adapter and independently grounded target replay. The explicit PROPOSED/PENDING fields are consistent with that limit.
limitations: Shape rejection is not a counterexample to the underlying mathematical statement.
No target expectation or semantic transport checker was fabricated to obtain admission.

findings.finding: Seven score companions fail the owning current-byte/evidence checker; ten more cite evidence outside the original inventory.
findings.impact: A displayed score token can remain arithmetically valid while its source or evidence binding is stale. Current-byte acceptance must check both.
limitations: No grade deservedness review was substituted for reading the cited evidence.
Outside the original inventory means unresolved in this audit; it is not asserted absent from all historical storage.
All three source-pin and eight distinct score-evidence-pin mismatches persist against LF normalization and pinned Git blobs.

findings.finding: Challenge manifests contain stale target hashes/sizes and inconsistent self-summary fields.
findings.impact: The listed custody cannot be treated as a currently validated judge packet. Several manifests explicitly disclaim being pre-run commitments.
limitations: CRLF_TO_LF normalization was applied only when explicitly declared; additional diagnostics show all 171 remaining mismatches persist in raw/LF/pinned-Git comparisons.
Unlisted-directory completeness and C011-C060 mathematical outputs were not certified.

findings.finding: Seven JSON evidence records have duplicate keys with conflicting values.
findings.impact: Ordinary JSON object loading silently chooses the last value, so these source inventories cannot represent a unique original path-to-digest map under a strict decoder.
limitations: No historical bytes were repaired.
A source relocation may explain conflicting names, but this audit does not establish the cause.

findings.finding: The normal-forms 25-test PASS receipt is not valid JSON; other parse failures include documented hostile or refused controls.

findings.impact: The normal-forms receipt requires preservation and a distinct corrected/replayed artifact before machine consumption. Intentional negative inputs must not be counted as damaged positive evidence.
limitations: The C057 checkers were not run on the hostile inputs here.
The claimed 25-test execution was not authenticated or rerun.

findings.finding: Most raw governed-run input mismatches are checkout line-ending effects; a smaller set remains different in the pinned Git content.
findings.impact: Do not interpret the large raw mismatch count as thousands of content changes. These remain historical receipts; content drift is limited here to the separately enumerated persistent mismatches.
limitations: A changed input hash is expected after source evolution and does not prove the earlier execution was false.
Referenced paths excluded from the original inventory were not opened.
Raw rule outcomes were preserved and qualified by per-file diagnostic indices; LF diagnostics do not silently change the declared hash convention.

validation.limit: A zero script exit means the audit completed and recorded failures, not that all evidence passed.
Fifteen positive/negative controls exercise selected parsers, owner score functions and digest functions; not exhaustive verification of this helper.
JSON-only readback. Original v1 provenance and injected proposal semantics were not replayed.

diagnostics.scope: Every mismatching in-inventory declared-hash/size reference plus all 108 v2 digest-named witness bundles. Outside-inventory references remain unresolved and were not opened.
diagnostics.limit: These diagnostics do not silently normalize accepted evidence or rewrite stored hashes. Original rule results retain their declared convention. Canonical payload/record digest failures are independent of checkout line endings.

rules.STRUCT: Parse every selected file and record duplicate keys; syntax only. YAML merges are allowed and explicit duplicate keys reported. JSON nonfinite/overflow numbers rejected. No data schema or semantic assertions follow.
rules.REF: Compare declared SHA-256 and optional size with current original-inventory bytes; declared CRLF_TO_LF is honored. No outside-inventory path is opened. Every reference and actual digest is in the references ledger.
rules.MAN: For 28 original judge manifests, normalize list/dict entries, resolve the manifest-wide declared base, count entries, compare bytes/sizes and recompute the explicitly defined C021 ordered-lines digest. No mathematical case-checker evaluation or full-directory completeness.
rules.SCORE: Invoke actual strict Pydantic models and owning score arithmetic, mutation ratio and current-byte checker without baseline grandfathering. Out-of-inventory evidence blocks only the corresponding custody check, not independent arithmetic.
rules.RUN: Invoke strict RunRecord model, compare recorded timestamps and every listed in-inventory input/report digest. Exit status is recorded, not silently required to be success. Executions are historical assertions.
rules.TOWER: Apply producer-defined no-float canonical bytes, content filenames, loss commitments/counts, declared census/status arithmetic, bundle-index links, fixture hashes, payload/record envelopes and provenance separation. Separately invoke the receiving closed schema; no receiving semantic replay.
rules.DERIV: Reconcile all retained v1 JSON terminal/snapshot/receipt records, exact token sums, decimal cost ceiling, prompt/request/raw hashes, configured model, settled attempts and sequence uniqueness. Read the experiment adapter before handling its reservation rules. No database/observer/runtime/provider execution.

file_reviews.assessment: Read the full checkout policy. Governed source and evidence paths generally request LF, with explicit raw-byte workflow exceptions. Diagnosed every failing reference against raw checkout bytes, CRLF-to-LF bytes and the original inventory Git blob; raw-byte failure is not automatically a content failure.

Read all model definitions, score/mutation arithmetic, evidence binding, baseline policy and CLI paths. Invoked strict Companion and RunRecord models and check_source for eligible records without grandfathering. The checker authenticates no execution; _run_problems only rejects a source hash if that source happens to be present among inputs, and does not itself verify every run input/report or require a zero exit status. Grades still require evidential judgment.

Read the entire acceptance policy. L4/D runtime and L2/D test floors are policy gates, not mathematical soundness conditions; baseline and exact empty-marker exceptions are explicitly separate from audited score arithmetic.

Read strict duplicate/float/nonfinite handling, canonical ASCII/LF encoding, rational normalization and domain-separated hashing. Audit serializer checked against these actual functions. Canonical bytes and hashes bind syntax only.

Read receipt-row construction, filename hash check, per-carrier uniqueness, coverage/depth arithmetic and canonical JSONL output. D counts contiguous admitted lifts and D_native is hard-coded zero; no reach receipt/checker context was executed by this supplemental audit.
Read closed object, exact integer versus Boolean, digest and canonical-rational admission. Invoked its validate function with transport.CERTIFICATE for every historical generated transport record.

Read producer/receiver envelope and ledger commitments, closed receiving certificate schema, exact finite injectivity checks, square equality and standing-loss obligations. Generated historical records fail the receiving shape before these semantic obligations; source records are not target-admission receipts.

Read all historical v1 bundle/evidence/loss/certificate builders. Audited loss histograms, producer-specific commitments, fixture digests, and proposed/pending ceilings. External vendor and historical engine imports were not re-executed; the supplied challenge is explicitly not derived from the seed.

Read all current v2 builders and installed-resource provenance changes. Recomputed field-defined commitments and discriminated a vendor Git commit from installed-package bytes. Generated records still mark transport PROPOSED; no semantic preservation theorem follows from their map names.
Read no-float sorted JSON encoder/decoder, SHA-256 and Git blob functions. Its exact canonicalization justifies the producer-side hash recomputations; no write function was called.

Read complete fixture loading/mutation, hosted decisions, census probing, expected-outcome and near-miss/kill checks. census_json serializes a dictionary of declared census classes; only derived summary arithmetic was rechecked here, not the underlying witness search or oracle behavior.
Read deterministic generation of digest-named bundle/evidence/loss files and index links. This is the owning source for filename-as-SHA-256 checks. Build and any vendor/model work were not invoked.
Read compact UTF-8 canonicalization, SHA-256, write-once semantics and checkout/resource discovery. Only the declared v1 byte conventions were reproduced; write_once was never invoked.

Read entire durable adapter and both historical v1 and current v2 replay paths. Applied JSON-only receipt/token/cost/reservation equations to every retained v1 run. Database comparison, injected observer replay, prompt regeneration, source imports and actual provider dispatch remain outside this audit.

Read per-stage decoding and max-output override, decimal price ceiling and timeout logic. Experiment reservations use ceiling(rate*hold*1e6), so applying the free-route reservation-zero rule to all v1 runs would be wrong; the final audit respects the recorded experiment profile.

Read bounded strict provider JSON object admission, duplicate-key rejection, nonfinite rejection, token integer constraints and optional reported cost. Arithmetic over a stored provider-shaped response cannot establish external provider authenticity.

Read all tests, including exact raw-byte manifest size/hash rules, checker agreement and syntactic independence checks. Used only the explicit manifest rule as a representative schema. Mathematical solver/checker tests were not run here; absence of cross-imports alone is not independent evidential validation.

Read all inventory, manifest, gauge/relabel, dual-checker, mutation and hostile-type tests. Its current 44-case assertion supersedes stale 46-case prose; the manifest hash/size convention was reviewed without rerunning mathematical checkers.

Read the complete claimed 25-test PASS receipt. Line 159 has a bare string without a property/value separator, so the artifact is not JSON. Its broad named mathematical claims are not established by the record or by this syntax finding; the named test execution was not rerun.
